title: Span Watermark & Backpressure Controller for Exporters
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Problem: During backend congestion (Tempo/Jaeger or third-party OTLP sinks) we currently drop spans or block ingestion threads leading to transient 5xx errors, skewed latency dashboards, and missing traces for customer investigations. Root causes observed: unbounded in-flight span buffers per tenant, no exporter-side watermark for stale spans, and lack of a standardized backpressure signal to the ingress/collector.

Goal: Implement a controller that enforces polite backpressure and span watermarks at the exporter level so that slow or unhealthy backends do not cause system-wide instability while preserving high-value trace fidelity for SLO-relevant requests.

Proposed design:
- Per-backend and per-tenant in-flight window with soft/hard watermarks: soft watermark (e.g., 75% capacity) triggers shed/priority mode; hard watermark (100%) starts TTL eviction of oldest non-critical spans.
- Span priority tagging: preserve high-priority spans (sampling markers: error=true, latency>p95, explicit trace_debug) through a separate reserved buffer.
- Adaptive backpressure signal: exporter emits metrics and an upstream gRPC health/backpressure header (X-Exporter-Backpressure) consumed by collector router to slow sampling, throttle non-critical ingest routes, or redirect to fallback sink (archive S3). Use exponential backoff with jitter.
- Watermark TTL eviction: spans older than configured TTL (default 30s) are dropped from main buffer and recorded as 'dropped_by_watermark' metric with tenant and backend labels.
- Observability: add 3 dashboards and alerting rules: exporter-buffer-heatmap, per-tenant-drop-rate, exporter-latency-and-retry. Emit traces for controller decisions to aid debugging.
- Compatibility: implement as a middleware layer inside the OTLP relay so it works for both HTTP and gRPC exporters and can be toggled per-backend via console config (Observability -> Exporters).

Acceptance criteria:
1) No global ingestion thread stalls observed during simulated backend slowdowns in staging (load test with 3x normal ingestion rate). 2) Drop-rate metrics are emitted per-tenant and match simulated drops. 3) High-priority spans retained at >99% under congestion. 4) Backpressure headers correctly set and upstream router reduces sample rate in e2e test. 5) Dashboard panels populated and alert fires when drop_rate > 0.5% for 5m.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for buffer state machine and TTL eviction (CI required).  - Integration test harness that replays golden traces and simulates backend latency/loss.  - Canary rollout to staging cluster, then to a single low-traffic prod region for 48h with monitoring.  - Gradual ramp to all regions after smoke validation.  - Provide migration notes for customers relying on exact trace counts; drops will be labeled and archived where possible.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: mis-tagging priority spans could cause loss of critical traces. Mitigation: conservative default priority rules and a feature flag to preserve all error spans until we verify. - Risk: backpressure signal creates oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis and stable backoff window, and observe with dashboards before full rollout.
